singleton.scenario: The cart and a background job each create a settings store and see different flag values.
singleton.request: Let both entry points share one in-process settings store.
singleton.problem: An unrestricted constructor creates independent state every time. Passing one object around can share it, but does not constrain future construction.
singleton.solution: Hide direct construction and let the class return its retained instance through one access point. This example guarantees uniqueness only within its JS runtime or Python process, not across distributed workers or concurrent initialization.
benefits: Shared state no longer diverges through repeated construction.
Creation and lifetime management have one owner.
Callers can coordinate a genuinely shared in-process resource.
singleton.when: Use it for a truly singular in-process resource with a clearly defined lifetime.
singleton.avoid: Do not use it merely as a convenient global variable. Prefer injected lifetimes for test doubles, request isolation or concurrent contexts.
singleton.tradeoff: A global access point hides dependencies and retains state between calls. Tests need isolation and concurrent initialization needs synchronization.
singleton.remember: Singleton controls instance count; it is not permission to make everything global.

factory-method.scenario: A notification workflow prepares text and sends email, but constructs the email sender directly.
factory-method.request: Add SMS delivery while keeping the formatting and logging workflow.
factory-method.problem: Choosing concrete senders inside the workflow forces edits for each new channel. A simple factory centralizes that decision, but one function still owns every product choice.
factory-method.solution: Keep the workflow in a creator base class and make sender creation an overridable factory method. Email and SMS creators return products behind one interface; the base workflow invokes that method rather than constructing a concrete sender.
benefits: A new creator adds a channel without changing the workflow.
Products implement a common sending interface.
Each creator owns its construction parameters and initialization.
factory-method.when: Use it when a reusable creator workflow needs subclasses to choose different products.
factory-method.avoid: Avoid a creator hierarchy just to replace a single constructor call.
factory-method.tradeoff: Each product may require a creator subclass. This inheritance-based extension is different from a simple factory.
factory-method.remember: The workflow stays in the creator; subclasses decide the product through the factory method.

abstract-factory.scenario: A page constructs buttons and checkboxes independently. Switching themes changes the button but leaves the checkbox light.
abstract-factory.request: Switch the entire control family to dark without mixing themes.
abstract-factory.problem: Independent product selection leaves compatibility to callers. Widget kinds and themes are tangled, producing mismatched combinations.
abstract-factory.solution: Define a factory interface with methods for buttons and checkboxes. Light and dark factories produce consistent families. The page depends only on factory and product interfaces; replacing the factory replaces the family.
benefits: One factory keeps products within a consistent family.
The page does not depend on concrete themed products.
A new theme adds a factory while retaining the page workflow.
abstract-factory.when: Use it for multiple compatible product families that must switch together.
abstract-factory.avoid: For one product kind, a factory function or factory method is often enough. Frequently adding product kinds is awkward here.
abstract-factory.tradeoff: Adding a family is easy; adding a product kind changes the factory interface and every concrete factory.
abstract-factory.remember: Choose a factory once to obtain a compatible family.

builder.scenario: Export jobs accept positional arguments for format, header, compression and attachments. Calls are difficult to read.
builder.request: Add a report preset and combine several optional settings.
builder.problem: Long constructors invite misplaced arguments. Copied setup sequences let defaults drift between callers.
builder.solution: Use a builder to configure format and header step by step, then build a separate result. An optional director encapsulates a report recipe. Copy configuration on build so later changes do not mutate earlier results.
benefits: Named steps make construction intent explicit.
Recipes reuse a consistent setup sequence.
Construction is separated from the result, with one validation boundary.
builder.when: Use it for complex optional configuration or multiple representations from one construction sequence.
builder.avoid: Do not add a builder when a few named parameters already make the call clear.
builder.tradeoff: The mutable builder needs reuse and reset rules. Fluent chaining alone is not the pattern.
builder.remember: Turn an opaque constructor call into explicit construction steps.

prototype.scenario: An editor creates cards from an existing template with a title and a nested tag list.
prototype.request: Edit the copy's tags without changing the template.
prototype.problem: Assignment shares the entire reference. A shallow copy duplicates only the outer object, leaving nested tags shared.
prototype.solution: Let the prototype expose clone, copying configuration and duplicating nested state that must be independent. Callers copy the prototype without reconstructing it. Real object graphs also require policies for cycles, resource handles and noncopyable state.
benefits: Reuse a fully configured runtime template.
The object owns its copying policy.
Make independent versus shared state explicit.
prototype.when: Use it when construction is complex or a runtime-configured object must be copied without knowing its concrete type.
prototype.avoid: Avoid it for objects with noncopyable connections or threads, or when a simple constructor is clearer.
prototype.tradeoff: Deep copying can be expensive. Identity, shared fields and cycles need an explicit policy.
prototype.remember: Copy existing configuration, but separate the state that must be independent.
